differences.text: The draft is always the property/attribute `value` on the element (no controlled/uncontrolled pairing, no onChange callback): the native `input` event bubbles up from the input for every user edit, and property writes never fire it. `onSubmit`/`onStop` are the `tct-chat-submit` and `tct-chat-stop` events.

`status` is `status-type` plus `status-message`. The message is announced once through the shared announcer when it appears or changes (assertive for an error), never through a live region on the strip, which would re-announce on every re-render.

With no `input` or `send-button` content the composer renders a default tct-chat-composer-input and tct-chat-send-button, so `<tct-chat-composer></tct-chat-composer>` is a complete composer; upstream renders them when the props are absent. The defaults are removed as soon as the slot has content.

The keyboard focus ring is drawn around the whole body while the editor has keyboard focus and nothing for pointer focus (interaction modality), as upstream; `disabled` also keeps the Stop action operable so a running response can always be stopped.

core.chat-composer.notes: Size: the folder budget (all six elements) is the measured gzip size, 75.4 kB, plus about 10%; it includes the ICU message parser (about 33 kB) that every translating family bundles (see provisional-budgets.json), and the hover card, badge, button and popover the input and token use. Guides: [mwg:css] (layers, logical properties, concentric radius through custom properties); [mwg:accessible-web-components] (announcements through the shared announcer, roles through ElementInternals); [mwg:shadow-dom] (slots, contexts across roots).

differences.text:
DECISION: the editing surface is a contenteditable element (plaintext-only), not a textarea with an overlay. Inline tokens that wrap with the text, are selectable, copyable and deleted as a unit exist only inside an editable flow; an overlay has to mirror the textarea's wrapping, scroll offset, font metrics, selection and IME underlines in a second layer, and gets every one of them subtly wrong (caret above a chip, drift after a resize, no native undo for a token). The price of contenteditable is accepted and handled in code: the selection is read through getComposedRanges with the ShadowRoot.getSelection fallback and written with setBaseAndExtent; tokens are non-editable inline elements that `beforeinput` removes as a unit; plain-text paste is inserted by hand; an NBSP follows each token so the caret has a place after it; line breaks in engines without plaintext-only are inserted on `beforeinput`; the trailing newline needs a placeholder
. An engine without contenteditable=plaintext-only (Firefox 125 to 135, Tier 2) falls back to `true` with formatting commands prevented on `beforeinput`, verified by a test that forces the fallback.

The editable is `role="textbox"` with `aria-multiline` and the accessible name `label`, or `role="combobox"` (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`) while triggers are configured. The suggestion popup is a `popover="manual"` listbox in the same shadow root, so the ID references resolve; options are named by their label and grouped by `auxiliaryData.group`. A disabled input stays a focus stop (`aria-disabled`, not editable) so focus is not dropped when a send disables the composer while a reply streams.

Tokens are named for screen readers: a badge chip is `role="img"` named by its label (else its value), so the token is read as one unit where it sits in the draft. An expandable (pasted-text) chip is named with its line and character count; its hover card is a pointer enhancement outside the image and the keyboard route is Shift+Arrow to select the chip and Enter to expand.

IME-safe Enter [mwg:ime-safe-enter-submit]: a keydown with `isComposing` or `keyCode` 229 never submits, never recalls history and never chooses a suggestion, and a submit whose Enter also commits an IME candidate is swallowed (the `compositionend` guard covers Safari's ordering). Verified with real IME events through the Chrome DevTools protocol (`Input.imeSetComposition`), not only synthetic keydowns. The soft-keyboard hint is `enterkeyhint="send"` on the editable, overridable by the global attribute on the host; `preventDefault()` on `tct-chat-submit` turns Enter into a newline on a touch keyboard.

`handleRef` is the element itself (its methods); `onKeyDown` is the native event with capture-phase `preventDefault()` claiming a key; `hasHistory` is the inverted `no-history`; `pasteAsToken` is a controller (or `false`) plus the `no-paste-as-token` attribute; `triggers` is property only. The trigger-menu items are `{id, label, auxiliaryData}` and the source is any object with `search(query)` (sync or async) and optional `cancel()`, so a typeahead search source can be used directly.

The text is the Tecton body size, raised to a 16px floor only on iOS WebKit with a coarse pointer (the upstream iOS-zoom guard), the caret and selection follow the theme, the placeholder is drawn by a sibling element (a contenteditable has none) with `aria-hidden`, and the field grows to `max-rows` before it scrolls. A trigger menu is a Tecton popup surface anchored to the caret (a virtual point anchor).

requests.reason: Move the three platform probes that chat-composer/chat-composer.platform.ts and speech-recognition.ts carry (`supportsPlaintextOnly`, a `getComposedRanges` probe, the Web Speech `SpeechRecognition` constructor lookup) into the central feature registry (tct/no-feature-checks intends them to live there). The composer wraps them lazily and cached today, so the move is mechanical: export the same names from features.ts and re-point the imports.

core.chat-composer-input.notes: Guides: [mwg:ime-safe-enter-submit] (isComposing or keyCode 229 gate, verified with a real IME through CDP); [mwg:accessible-web-components] (textbox/combobox roles, aria-activedescendant inside one shadow root); [mwg:shadow-dom] (selection APIs across the shadow boundary: getComposedRanges, ShadowRoot.getSelection); [mwg:resilient-context-menus-and-nested-dropdowns] and [mwg:position-aware-tooltips] (a manual popover anchored to the caret, flipped by the shared position controller); [mwg:break-up-long-tasks] (the paste path and token pruning do bounded work); [mwg:privacy] (dictation: nothing is recorded or sent by the component, the microphone is requested only on user activation); [mwg:css].

hooks.notes: speech-recognition.ts: feature-detected Web Speech recognition with a microphone level meter (noise-floor calibrated bands). `subscribe()` delivers every per-frame level, the host update only the coarse state.

chat-dictation.ts: `new ChatDictationController(host, {input: () => composerInput})` writes interim text as a ghost line in the input, commits final text, turns caps lock on for sustained loud speech and plays optional cues.

differences.text: Dictation is feature-detected: without `SpeechRecognition` (Firefox) or `webkitSpeechRecognition` the controller reports `isSupported = false`, the button hides itself or (with `show-unsupported`) is disabled, and nothing throws. Permission denial, no-speech and a failed start end the session and reset the state; the microphone tracks, the frame loop and the recognition session are released on stop and when the host disconnects.

The equalizer bars are decoration (`aria-hidden`), their movement stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and the listening state is exposed by the button's changing name ("Start dictation" / "Stop dictation"). Recognition results reach the draft through the input, so a screen reader hears them as typed text.

core.chat-dictation-button.notes: Guides: [mwg:privacy] (the microphone is requested only after a user activation and released on stop; no audio leaves the component); [mwg:accessible-web-components]; [mwg:css]. Firefox has no Web Speech recognition, so the unsupported path is the tested default there.
